about.title: Sunnyvale Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Sunnyvale sits in the middle of Santa Clara County's commute grid, and its collision numbers reflect that. In 2025, the city's final tally showed 457 injury collisions, 603 people hurt, and 3 traffic deaths across a community of roughly 151,754 residents. Public records point to a handful of high-volume corridors: El Camino Real, SR-237, Mathilda Avenue, and Fair Oaks Avenue. Crashes here also cluster on Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when workday traffic is heaviest. If one of those numbers now describes your afternoon, the practical steps matter more than the statistics. Get checked by a doctor even if you feel shaken rather than injured, photograph the scene and vehicles, and hold onto every receipt. Politely decline when the other driver's insurer asks for a recorded statement before you have spoken with counsel. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent car accident attorney who handles Sunnyvale cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case produces a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Sunnyvale Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than They Look
items.desc: California gives most injury claims two years, but a crash involving a city vehicle, a county road defect, or a public transit bus may require a government claim in as little as six months. Connecting with an attorney early keeps those doors open.

items.title: Partial Blame Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly responsible for the collision; your share of fault simply reduces the amount. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your percentage.

items.title: No Fee Unless There Is a Recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life. You pay nothing to be connected and nothing to the attorney unless your case produces a recovery.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You are not required to, and it is usually wise to wait until you have talked with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift fault onto you or minimize your injuries. A simple, polite "I'd prefer to speak with a lawyer first" is enough.

items.question: I was rear-ended on SR-237 during Thursday evening traffic. What should I do now?
items.answer: Start by seeing a doctor, even if the soreness feels minor, because stop-and-go collisions often produce neck and back injuries that surface a day or two later. Save the police report number, your photos, and any dashcam footage, and write down what you remember while it is fresh. Then let us connect you with an attorney who can request records and deal with the insurers on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Sunnyvale?
items.answer: For most crashes in California, the statute of limitations is two years from the date of injury. If a government entity is involved, such as a city or county vehicle or a roadway maintenance issue on a public street like Mathilda Avenue, you may have only six months to file an administrative claim first. Because the clock varies, it is worth speaking with an attorney sooner rather than later.
